record.text: I also cannot emphasize enough how most LLM use in jobs is extremely rudimentary and crude. Very bad vibe coding abounds. Terrible documentation in vast amounts. I don’t love that. I used to have a job that placed major limits on my ability to use LLMs professionally. Within a few weeks of moving to a more “normal” tech job I’m probably 85% as proficient as my peers. I’m not that special. I’m not learning on my own time. I’m just using stuff at work to do work tasks.

A major reason I despise “don’t get left behind” rhetoric on LLMs is that it pretends learning is hard, and that there’s a first-mover advantage here. Poppycock. You can ignore the tools and later learn them - and spend less time learning stuff that’s made obsolete by frontier advancements in 6mo.
